name: M1 -> D85 reverted: the posterior floor never engages, so the budget spends the day's last hinge again and a leg day ships with no hip extension on it
anchor: if(_postLeft<=1 && _isPost(it.name)) return;       // V198 (D85): the day's LAST hinge/hip_ext is not budget fodder
replacement: if(false && _postLeft<=1 && _isPost(it.name)) return;       // V198 (D85): the day's LAST hinge/hip_ext is not budget fodder
note: A1a/A1b name the symptom directly: the day's only hinge is gone from the hand-computed after-list. A4, A5b/A5c and B3 also see it.

name: M2 -> the floor is raised from 1 to 2: a second posterior item is protected too, which is a volume decision nobody ruled and is not the nonempty/empty boundary
note: A2a/A2c: with two hinges on the day the later one must still be ordinary budget fodder.

name: M3 -> leg_iso folded into the posterior set: 'Leg extension', a pure quad movement that shares EXLIB.leg_accessory with Leg press, is now defended as posterior chain
note: A3a/A3b, the leg_iso control. This is the defect coach flagged in the measure pass's own E_POSTERIOR oracle.

name: M4 -> the count is precomputed before the trim loop instead of re-read inside it: the stale count still reads 2 after the first removal, so the second pass eats the day's last hinge anyway
note: A2b/A2c, the live-count proof: the day starts with two hinges and must finish with exactly one.

name: M5 -> the floor is implemented on the SECTION LABEL instead of on the day's items, the D50 failure repeated: a day whose posterior work sits under any other label is left unprotected
note: A2a/A2c. A label-keyed count reads 0 on the hand-built days (their hinge sits under 'Finisher', which is exactly the case a label floor cannot see), so 0<=1 protects EVERY posterior item and the two-hinge day refuses to give one up. Verified: M5 trips A2a and A2c.

name: M6 -> the rank-2 label set gains 'delt', so the shoulder prehab section becomes early fodder and the D85 trim lands OUTSIDE the four names the licence covers
note: B3 wide (D85 CONFINEMENT, no-baseline floor) is the named trip: off-licence prehab falls 330/426/394/333/333/291 -> 174/282/283/231/231/195, a loss of 711 on 6/6 tiers, while the four licensed names still fall exactly 661. That is the shape the licence exists to catch - a second, unruled regression walking in behind a ruled one. The V192 census floor does NOT catch it (every tier stays above 3711-3867), which is why the transcribed V197 off-licence table had to exist for sabotage to reach this claim at all.
